meta.title: Unique Talent: Amputee, Wheelchair User, Short-Statured & Distinctive Performers | Take 3 Agency
meta.description: Take 3 Agency represents professional performers with lived experience for film, television, commercials and modelling: amputee artists, wheelchair users, short-statured and very tall performers, people with vitiligo, tattooed and alternative looks, and distinctive faces. Trained professionals first, with accessibility considered from the first conversation.
meta.ogDescription: Professional performers who challenge conventional casting: amputee artists, wheelchair users, short-statured and very tall performers, distinctive faces and alternative looks, represented for everything they bring to a role.

hero.heading: Unique talent
hero.lede: Professional performers who challenge conventional casting, represented for everything they bring to a role: skill, training, presence and lived experience.

figure.alt: A black-and-white studio portrait of a performer with tattooed arms and painted eyes, hands raised to the face.

representation.heading: Space for all kinds of people
paragraphs: At Take 3, we believe an inclusive industry is one that makes space for all kinds of people, bodies, abilities and experiences. Film and television should reflect the world around us in all its individuality and diversity. We want to create opportunities for professional artists with lived experience to bring authentic representation to screen, while celebrating the qualities that make each artist unique.

Our Unique Talent roster celebrates the people who challenge conventional casting: from extreme and varying heights to distinctive faces, alternative looks, amputees, wheelchair users, tattooed talent, characterful performers and artists with unique physicality.

Whether their background is in dance, action, modelling, acting or specialist performance, they are highly skilled, trained professionals first and foremost. That is what makes the work authentically inclusive, rather than a box ticked.

figure.alt: A black-and-white studio photograph of a performer folded forward at the waist, arms stretched behind them, in a sheer patterned top and heavy boots.

roster.heading: Celebrated for who they are. Cast for what they can do.

items.title: Height and stature
items.body: Performers at the far ends of the range, from very tall to short-statured, cast for roles written around their height and for smaller doubling work, and represented as actors rather than as a measurement.

items.title: Amputee artists and wheelchair users
items.body: Performers with limb difference and wheelchair users, working as actors, doubles, models and background across major productions, with their access needs understood long before anyone reaches set.

items.title: Distinctive faces and alternative looks
items.body: Heavily tattooed talent, striking bone structure, vitiligo, scarring, natural hair and looks a standard casting call rarely reaches: faces that hold a frame and stay with an audience.

items.title: Characterful performers and unique physicality
items.body: Performers whose presence, movement or physicality is unmistakably their own, for productions and brands that want believable over polished and memorable over neutral.
SPACT doubles for child characters, bringing the required size, physicality and stunt ability together.
Heavily tattooed and alternative-looking artists, cast for the faces a standard call rarely reaches.
Interesting, distinctive faces booked for modelling and background roles.
Amputee artists working across major productions, and Wheelchair Barbie and Amputee Barbie bringing lived experience to the world of Barbieland.
Doubles matched on height, build and physicality when a standard double cannot be found.

accessibility.heading: Considered from the first conversation
paragraphs: We believe accessibility should be considered from the first conversation, not once an artist arrives on set.
We work closely with access specialists to develop our understanding of both visible and non-visible access needs, and to ensure our artists are supported throughout the casting and booking process.
Every artist is different. There is no one-size-fits-all approach to accessibility, so we focus on individual needs, clear communication and practical solutions.

support.heading: Cast the talent. Support the individual.
support.body: If you are casting an artist with an access requirement, our team can help facilitate the conversation between artist and production.
